title: Incident Anticipation and Rapid Triage Sprint Guide
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:
This guide prescribes a compact, repeatable process to anticipate common failure modes, run short triage sprints, and deliver consistent customer-facing status updates. It is targeted at responders (first-on-call engineers, SRE/Platform), service owners, and the incident bridge operator. Use this as a canonical checklist for incidents where fast containment and measured customer comms are the priority (Priority P1/P2).

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood inference services: API gateway, serving runtime, autoscaler, and KV cache layers.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks; instead, it prescribes the sprint and coordination primitives used to invoke runbooks and communicate externally.

Key objectives:
1) Restore a safe operating envelope within 15 minutes for P1 events (partial or full service outage).
2) Provide a clear status narrative to customers and leadership within 30 minutes.
3) Capture structured evidence for a postmortem within 72 hours.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- First Responder: acknowledge alerts, run diagnostics, escalate to Bridge if unresolved in 10 minutes.
- Bridge Operator: orchestrates communications, opens bridge (Zoom/Slack huddle), publishes status page updates, owns incident timeline.
- Service Owner: advises on rollback/runbook steps, signs any tenant-impacting changes.
- SRE Lead: approves cross-service mitigations (traffic shifts, capacity reallocation).

Incident classification matrix (summary):
| Severity | Symptoms | Immediate target | Bridge required |
| P0 | Total outage affecting >= 90% of traffic | 15 min restore or mitigation | Yes (full incident bridge) |
| P1 | Significant degradation impacting core customers | Contain in 15 min, restore in 1 hour | Yes |
| P2 | Partial, non-critical degradation | Fix within 24 hours | Optional |
(When in doubt classify conservatively — prefer P1 for multi-tenant customer-facing regressions.)

Rapid Triage Sprint — checklist (first 15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge & annotate: first responder sets incident labels (service, region, error class) in the incident tracker and records initial symptoms (top logs, recent deploys).
2) Bridge & channel: Bridge Operator creates incident channel (Slack #bridge-<id>) and a temporary doc (Incident Sprint Sheet) with visible fields: severity, impacted customers, start time, first actions.
3) Quick smoke tests: run the canonical health-check and the top 3 synthetic queries used in SLO monitoring.
4) Verify recent changes: CI/CD deploys (last 60m), infra changes, config pushes.
5) Execute containment if safe: scale up dedicated pool, disable autoscaler bursts, or activate read-only mode for internal control plane. Document every step.

Runbook invocation pattern (how to call service runbooks):
- When a triage sprint identifies a root cause candidate, follow "One-Action Rule": take one safe mitigation (e.g., redirect traffic) and observe for five minutes. No two independent risky changes in parallel.
- Push results to the Incident Sprint Sheet with precise command lines and config diffs. Include expected rollback steps.

Escalation ladder (timed):
1) T+0–10m: Escalate to Bridge if triage unresolved.
2) T+10–30m: Bring in Service Owner and SRE Lead.
3) T+30–60m: Executive on-call notified for P0/P1 if customer impact persists; start cross-service mitigation run.

Evidence collection & quick-forensics checklist:
- Snapshot logs (5 minute windows) for gateway, runtime, autoscaler.
- Capture top 20 noisy stack traces and error keys.
- Snapshot metrics (qps,  p50/p95 latency, error rate) and recent config state (feature flags, host pools).
- Preserve the failing VM/container/actor for postmortem if possible.

Status page & customer communications templates (use verbatim where applicable):
Template: Short initial status (for status.redwood.ai and customer emails)
Subject: "[Status] Degraded inference responses — investigating (service: <service>, region: <region>)"
Body:
We are aware of degraded responses affecting <service> in <region>. Our engineers are investigating. Impact: some requests may fail or be delayed. Next update: <T+30m>. If you are seeing significant customer impact please reply to this message or contact support@redwood.ai with your tenant id.

Template: 30-minute update (if mitigations in progress)
Subject: "[Update] Mitigation underway — partial recovery observed"
Body:
Mitigation: We have applied <mitigation> (e.g., increased dedicated pool, routed traffic away from noisy host). We are seeing partial recovery: success rate improved from X% to Y% and latency p95 reduced from A ms to B ms. We continue to monitor across regions. Estimated next update: <T+60m>.

Template: Post-incident customer summary (short)
Subject: "[Resolved] Service disruption affecting <service> — summary and impact"
Body:
Summary: The incident began at <start time> and was resolved at <end time>. Root cause: <short cause>. Impact: <brief impact numbers> (e.g., 12% of requests failed, customers in EU-1 experienced elevated latency). Mitigation: <actions taken>. Actions we will take: <1–3 concrete actions and timeline>. If you need tenant-specific evidence contact your CSM.

Game day / Simulation playbook (biweekly micro-sprints):
Purpose: validate rapid triage and status cadence without disrupting production.
Plan (45–90 minutes):
- Pregame: select an injected failure (e.g., KV cache eviction storm, autoscaler underrun, model fallback error) and verify synthetic monitors fire.
- Execution: first responder runs through the Rapid Triage Sprint checklist; Bridge Operator publishes two status updates (initial & 30m).
- Postgame: 30 min retrospective focusing on comms clarity and time-to-first-action.
Metrics to capture: time-to-ack, time-to-bridge, time-to-first-mitigation, quality of status message (peer-rated).

Rotation cadence & handoff template:
- Primary oncall: 7-day cadence for responders in SRE/Platform team.
- Secondary: 7-day cadence offset by 3 days to ensure overlap.
- Bridge duty: weekly rotation for engineers signed up on Bridge roster.
Handoff checklist (before stepping down):
1) Confirm no active incidents or hand over open bridges with a summary.
2) Share any ongoing mitigations, TTLs on rate limits, and next scheduled tasks.
3) Update the oncall calendar and incident tracker with notes.

Postmortem scaffold (must be completed within 72 hours):
- Title, severity, start/end timestamps, services impacted, customer impact notes.
- Timeline: minute-level timeline for first hour, 5–15 minute buckets thereafter.
- Root cause analysis: short causal chain and why safeguards failed.
- Remediation plan: owner, priority, due date.
- Lessons learned & runbook updates required (link to runbook).
- Evidence attachments: logs, dashboard snapshots, code/config diffs.

Runbook hygiene & ownership:
- Every runbook must declare: owner (persona), last-reviewed date, and a test vector (synthetic query and expected response).
- Quarterly review: owners run a live validation during a game day.
- Deprecation policy: if no owner or no test vector for >6 months mark runbook for retirement.

Operational metrics & SLO tie-ins to track after incidents:
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) target: < 2 minutes for pager alerts.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM): < 15 minutes for P1.
- Post-incident action completion rate: 100% tracked to owners within 30 days.

Appendix: Useful commands & dashboards (examples)
- CI/CD: curl -sS https://ci.redwood.ai/api/v1/latest-deploys?service=<service>
- Health checks: curl -sS https://<service>.<region>.redwood.ai/ready | jq .status
- Dashboards: torq.redwood.ai/d/serving/runtime-overview and torq.redwood.ai/d/alerts/incident-runner

Related links & references:
- Incident evidence policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-evidence-policy
- SLO catalog: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets

Ownership & review cycle:
- Document owner: Maya Chen (SRE) — quarterly review.
- Reviewers: Arjun Patel (Platform), Lucia Gomez (Support), Noah Stein (Service Reliability).

If you have suggestions for this sprint guide or want to run a custom game day scenario, open a PR against this page or ping #sre-runbook-maintainers.
